semantics.note: 'Will poke' and 'surely find' are firm language, so this is a scored forecast. The 'may fall short' hedge earlier in the paragraph applies to the order's effectiveness, not to this sentence.

contract.note: The plain reading (companies seeking and identifying exploitable gaps) is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly says that analyst critiques alone and rescission alone settle nothing.

evidence.note: Primary record of EO 14148 revoking EO 14110 on 2025-01-20. It bounds the period but says nothing about company conduct on loopholes.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet holds no documented episode of companies seeking and finding EO 14110 loopholes, and no comprehensive record showing the opposite. Rescission limits the period but proves neither outcome. The evidence does not settle it.

semantics.note: Describes what the order contained. The 'probably not enough' part is hedged and has no standard, so it is not scored. Only breadth and 'some teeth' are adjudicable.

contract.note: Reading 'broad' as covering current harms plus advanced-AI risks, and 'some teeth' as mandatory DPA-based directions, is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly sets aside the adequacy judgment.

evidence.note: Official text of the order, dated 2023-10-30. It covers privacy, discrimination, consumer and worker harms, and per the cited sections, advanced-model risks and DPA-based information requirements.

Same-day White House fact sheet describing the mandatory DPA reporting and red-team disclosure. It is the government describing its own order, but it matches the order text. The 'news_report' label is minor mislabeling.

reviews.rationale: The order's text addresses current harms (privacy, civil rights, consumers, workers) and advanced-model risks, and directs Commerce to require company reporting under the DPA. That supports 'broad' and 'some teeth'. The hedged 'probably not enough' adequacy judgment is not adjudicable and was not scored.
